canonical_label.bijection_note: t is the discrete log of y base g, hence a bijection Z/r -> <g>; a canonical-label collision and an element collision are the same event
canonical_label.definition: t = a + x*b mod r with y = g^a z^b and z = g^x

derivation.claim: the record key is a function of the state (y, guard); the canonical label (t, guard) is in bijection with (y, guard), so a key collision on the canonical g^a z^b label IS a state collision, and vice versa. The shipped 48-byte class key is COARSER (twelve Frobenius partners share it), so element repeats imply key repeats but not conversely; the solve enumerates the twelve shifts, and the trap charge counts the finer (element, guard) event, which is the conservative side.
derivation.direction: element/label repeat => key repeat (never the reverse implication is used)

note: fixture-scale relabel witness only. The production census in evidence/repeat-classes-v19.json counts (element, guard) repeats over 1e6 step pairs; by the bijection above those are exactly the canonical g^a z^b label repeats, so the v20 trap numbers (1744 nonzero-increment / 0 zero-increment) are unchanged and the relabel is a derivation, not a recount.

solvability_split.rule: a repeat with delta-b = 0 mod r makes the collision equation independent of x (a1 + b x = p^j(a2 + b x) has no x term when b1 = b2), so it is UNSOLVABLE: the v18 trap class. delta-b != 0 gives one equation in x per shift and is solvable.
